open_decision: The laws do not fix the order of the new entries among themselves (nor how many times each is appended): RowsKept only makes the old registry a prefix.
input: enable=true, locked=(fun _ => false), registry=[], starters=[{id:1,adapter:1,model:1,enabled:true},{id:2,adapter:2,model:2,enabled:true}] (distinct ids, both absent)
result_b: design that appends the adjusted absent entries in reverse starter order: [{id:2,adapter:2,model:2,enabled:true},{id:1,adapter:1,model:1,enabled:true}]
reason: Both designs keep the registry as a prefix, add exactly the absent starters with the right enabled flag, so they pass every law. No law constrains the order of the appended part, so the results differ.
